records.name: Philadelphia Orchard Project
records.summary: A nonprofit that plants and cares for community orchards across Philadelphia, working with schools, churches, and community gardens. Anyone can help at its open work days.
records.what_you_do: Dig, plant, mulch, prune, and weed at orchard work days, and help with workshops and events.

schedule.text: Weekly Tuesday work days at the Learning Orchard at The Woodlands, a monthly open orchard afternoon, and seasonal planting days

locations.label: POP Learning Orchard at The Woodlands

cost.text: No volunteer fee is listed for individuals

first_step.how: Join the volunteer email list or register for a work day on the events page
first_step.basis: Work days need no experience, and the site explains how to register

records.notes: Groups of 5 to 10 is the most POP can take, and groups of 15 or more are not accepted. Partner orchard list and Penn Park, Hort Center and Awbury workdays are on the same site.

records.name: Bartram's Garden
records.summary: A historic garden on the Schuylkill River in Southwest Philadelphia. Its Sankofa Community Farm grows food with volunteers, who also help with festivals and movie nights.
records.what_you_do: Weed, plant, and harvest at the farm and garden, and help run public events such as festivals, movie nights, and Saturday activities.

schedule.text: Welcome Volunteer shifts of about 3 hours, mostly at public events, with at least 3 shifts per season from May to October. Upcoming: farm volunteer day Sat Oct 10 at 9:30 am and horticulture volunteer day Sat Oct 17 at 9:30 am

locations.label: Bartram's Garden and Sankofa Community Farm

cost.text: No fee listed; Welcome Volunteers receive a free one-year membership

first_step.how: Welcome Volunteer applications are closed right now, so sign up on the notify list; each volunteer registers for shifts individually
first_step.basis: The way in is closed at the time of checking and needs a waiver and a sign up before the first shift

records.notes: The volunteer page lists upcoming days without a year. Oct 10 and Oct 17 fall on Saturdays in 2026, so the year was inferred from the weekday. Recheck when Welcome Volunteer applications reopen.

records.name: Awbury Food Forest
records.summary: A food forest in Awbury Arboretum in Germantown, looked after by a volunteer group with support from the Philadelphia Orchard Project. Volunteers join work days to care for the plantings.
records.what_you_do: Join morning work days to tend the trees and plantings, along with the other volunteers.

schedule.text: Work days listed on the Orchard Project calendar; the next one is Wed Oct 14, 9 am to 12 pm

first_step.how: Register for a work day on the Orchard Project events page, or email volunteer@awbury.org
first_step.basis: Work days are public and have a clear sign up step

records.notes: The Awbury website does not describe the food forest group itself, so the workday facts come from the Orchard Project events page. The Awbury site shows two different phone numbers, so no phone is recorded. The Beekeepers Guild site lists the apiary at The Farm at Awbury, which is a separate place from the food forest.

records.name: Philadelphia Beekeepers Guild
records.summary: Beekeepers and bee lovers who promote sustainable urban beekeeping through monthly meetings, a shared apiary, and a yearly honey festival.
records.what_you_do: Come to monthly meetings to learn beekeeping, join the group's work at its apiary, and help with the honey festival.

schedule.text: Monthly meetings on the third Thursday at 7 pm

first_step.how: Come to a monthly meeting, or join through the Join Us page or mailing list
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to the public and the site names a clear way to join

records.notes: The site lists a 2026 Honey Fest recap but shows no date for it, so the status is probably_active rather than active. The 2015 article about St. James School meetings is older and was not used for the current place.

records.name: Community Gardens Network (Farm Philly)
records.summary: The city's network of 19 community gardens on park land, where about 500 residents grow food together. Farm Philly provides land access, compost, mulch, supplies, workshops, and training.
records.what_you_do: Grow food in a shared garden, swap skills with other growers, and help with community programs at the garden.

schedule.text: Set by each garden; find a garden on the city's map or email farmphilly@phila.gov

cost.text: The page does not mention fees

first_step.how: Find a garden on the city's map of registered sites and contact it, or email farmphilly@phila.gov
first_step.basis: The page gives a clear way to find and contact a garden

records.notes: The page has no dates. The Carousel House Farm and its CSA are suspended until further notice, so they are not recorded here. The page also mentions Junior Farmers, a program for ages 5 to 15 at 20 recreation centers, which is not separately recorded.

records.name: Philly Peace Park
records.summary: A neighborhood-run ecology campus with two urban farms in North and West Philadelphia. It offers free farming, education, and health programs.
records.what_you_do: Help on the farms, take part in free education and wellness programs, and shop at the weekly Black Market.

schedule.text: Monthly Self-Care Saturdays and a weekly market; the site does not list volunteer days

first_step.how: Email phillypeacepark@gmail.com; the site does not describe a volunteer process
first_step.basis: The site gives an email but no clear way to start volunteering

records.notes: The home page gives a different Jefferson Street address (930 N 51st or 2216 W Jefferson) from the footer (2200 W Jefferson), so verify before publishing. Footer copyright and image dates are not treated as evidence. No dated posts were found.

records.name: Philadelphia Master Gardeners
records.summary: A volunteer program run through Penn State Extension. Trained volunteers answer gardening questions, give talks, and care for public demonstration gardens around Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: After training, volunteers staff a gardening help line, speak to groups, and work in demonstration and youth gardens.

schedule.text: Training runs each fall into spring, with weekly virtual lectures from October to March and monthly in-person classes. Volunteers then give 50 hours in the first year and 20 hours a year after.

first_step.how: Attend an online information session, then apply to the training class
first_step.basis: Applicants must attend an information session and apply before training starts

records.notes: Facts come from search excerpts. The training page moved (301 redirect, then a 404 at the new address), so it was not read in full. The 2025 class dates are the newest found. Check the 2026 class and cost before publishing. The coordinator name in the search result may be out of date and is not recorded.

records.name: Horticulture Center Food Forest
records.summary: An educational food forest at the Fairmount Park Horticulture Center, built by Parks and Recreation, Penn State Master Gardeners, and the Orchard Project. Volunteers weed and care for the plantings at work days.
records.what_you_do: Join afternoon work days to weed and tend the food forest plantings, with tools and water provided.

schedule.text: Work days posted on the Orchard Project events page; the next one is Wed Oct 14, 2 to 4 pm

locations.label: Fairmount Park Horticulture Center food forest

cost.text: No fee listed for work days

first_step.how: Register for a work day on the Orchard Project events page
first_step.basis: Work days are public and need an advance registration

records.notes: The events page lists no street address for this food forest. The address 100 N Horticultural Dr comes from a 2025 Penn Today event listing that was seen in a search excerpt, not fetched. Email is the Orchard Project's general address, since this food forest has no page of its own.
